articles.summary: KYIV: Ukraine attacked a Russian oil refinery Thursday, abandoning a brief truce involving energy-related targets that it said Moscow did not heed, as
articles.body: KYIV: Ukraine attacked a Russian oil refinery Thursday, abandoning a brief truce involving energy-related targets that it said Moscow did not heed, as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he felt betrayed by US President Trump. The drone strike started a fire at the refinery about 300 kilometers southeast of Moscow in Russia's Ryazan region, according to the Russian defence ministry and Ryazan governor Pavel Malkov. Russia's Astra online news outlet posted what it said was a photograph of the blaze. The strike could further complicate Kyiv's relations with Trump, which have soured again in recent days amid deepening tensions with Washington.Zelenskyy said he was outraged by Russia's continuing aerial bombardment of his country's energy infrastructure in apparent defiance of Trump's demand on Sunday for both sides to halt those attacks.Despite going along with Trump's demand for a truce, Zelensky complained, Ukraine in recent days was denied the usual Western intelligence on Russian ballistic missile strikes, and limits were placed on its use of US-made Starlink communication terminals. Both are vital for the Ukrainian military.He said his patience had run out, telling the Financial Times in an interview published Thursday that Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries would resume. "We're done," Zelenskyy was quoted as saying.A senior Ukrainian official confirmed that Ukraine had hit the refinery. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Thursday that Ukraine never stopped its strikes on refineries that have hurt Russia. It wasn't possible to independently verify each side's claims.Amid fears that the Trump administration may be withdrawing support for Ukraine, Zelenskyy went to Brussels Thursday for talks with EU leaders attending a two-day summit. Zelenskyy said he would meet with Nato chief Mark Rutte, French President Emmanuel Macron, and the PMs of Poland, Denmark and Belgium.In other developments, three people were killed and six others injured after the Kirovohrad region of central Ukraine came under a Russian drone attack lasting more than 10 hours, Ukraine's emergency services said Thursday.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ukraine runs out of US-made Patriot interceptors amid mounting Russian attacks: Report
articles.summary: Ukraine has run out of missiles for its US-made Patriot air defence systems, leaving it vulnerable to Russian ballistic missile attacks, CNN reported
articles.body: Ukraine has run out of missiles for its US-made Patriot air defence systems, leaving it vulnerable to Russian ballistic missile attacks, CNN reported citing a source familiar with the situation.The shortage comes amid mounting pressure on US weapons stocks, tensions between Washington and Kyiv over attacks on Russian energy infrastructure, and uncertainty over continued American military support.According to CNN, Ukraine's shortage of Patriot interceptors left almost all Russian ballistic missiles in the latest overnight attack unintercepted.The strikes hit three power plants in Kyiv and targeted energy infrastructure in Kharkiv, killing four people and injuring 25 in the Ukrainian capital. The shortage has raised concerns about Ukraine's ability to protect critical infrastructure as Russia continues its attacks on the country's energy network.The interceptors are expensive and in short supply globally, with countries depleting their stockpiles or seeking to replenish their air defence systems amid the ongoing war involving Iran. The shortage has intensified concerns over Washington's ability to meet Ukraine's requirements while addressing its own military needs and those of its allies.The shortage has coincided with a sharp deterioration in relations between US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, following Washington's controversial deal to import Russian diesel and Trump's push for an energy ceasefire between Moscow and Kyiv.Zelenskyy has accused Russia of continuing attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure despite Kyiv temporarily halting strikes on Russian oil facilities in response to the proposal.The dispute has extended beyond weapons supplies to US intelligence and satellite communications. Ukrainian officials told CNN they had not received the early-warning alerts about Russian ballistic missile launches that had previously helped authorities warn civilians to seek shelter.Separately, restrictions affecting Starlink connectivity used by Ukrainian military drones disrupted some offensive and defensive operations. Elon Musk said decisions on military-grade Starshield access rest with the US government, highlighting Kyiv's dependence on American-controlled technology.

articles.title: Remove Dushyant Kumar Gautam as Sikkim governor in 24 hours or face nationwide stir: Rishikesh resort murder victim's dad
articles.summary: DEHRADUN/NEWDELHI: Hours after Delhi Police detained them during a pre-dawn protest at India Gate on Thursday, the parents of the 2022 Rishikesh resort
articles.body: DEHRADUN/NEWDELHI: Hours after Delhi Police detained them during a pre-dawn protest at India Gate on Thursday, the parents of the 2022 Rishikesh resort murder victim vowed to intensify their fight for justice, with her father giving a 24-hour ultimatum for the removal of Dushyant Kumar Gautam as Sikkim governor.He threatened a nationwide agitation beginning in Delhi if the demand was not met.The family sought an appointment with President Droupadi Murmu, while leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi wrote to her separately, urging reconsideration of Gautam’s appointment until CBI completed its investigation.Speaking to TOI after his release, the victim’s father said, “We want to meet the President and have made an appeal to meet her to narrate our agony. We were removed from the protest but this is not the end.” He added, “We will be staying in the national capital and wait before proceeding further in the matter.”The father reiterated that Gautam should not hold the post of governor while the investigation was on. Referring to the unresolved questions surrounding the alleged involvement of a “VVIP” in his daughter’s death, he added, “The name of the VVIP still remains a mystery. Once the CBI investigation ends, all the facts will come to the fore.”In his letter to President Murmu, Rahul argued that constitutional immunity attached to the governor’s office could prevent criminal proceedings against Gautam during his tenure. “An inquiry that can never result in prosecution is an inquiry in name only,” he wrote.President Murmu appointed Gautam, a former BJP Uttarakhand in-charge, as Sikkim governor on Oct 12.The murder case involved allegations that a VIP had demanded “special service” from the victim, who allegedly refused. Her body was found in a canal. The resort belonged to the son of a then BJP neta. Gautam’s name had figured in the allegations concerning the purported VIP, but these remain unproven.The victim’s parents began protesting at India Gate on Wednesday evening, where Rahul, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and party general secretary KC Venugopal joined them. Several Congress netas were part of the overnight demonstration.Around 4am Thursday, Delhi Police detained the parents, activist Yogita Bhayana and several Congress members, taking them to Tilak Nagar police station. Party workers protested the action, while videos circulated showing many attempting to block the bus carrying detainees. Police later released the parents.Asked about Congress netas joining their protest, the victim’s father told TOI, “We had not invited anyone. On hearing that we were protesting, they came to extend support.” He said the couple had met Rahul at his Delhi residence earlier. “He had assured us support in our fight for justice,” he said.Uttarakhand’s women and child welfare minister Rekha Arya, however, accused Congress of politicising the case. “Securing justice for the family is a matter linked to the emotions of the entire state of Uttarakhand and the dignity of daughters. It is unfortunate to use this sensitive matter for political gain,” she said.Questioning Congress’s protests in Delhi and Dehradun, Arya asked whether the party genuinely wanted justice for the victim’s family or was attempting to regain its lost political ground. “It is easy to do politics in the name of a daughter, but to secure justice, one has to stand with solid facts, evidence and the legal process,” she said.Arya maintained that the state govt had acted swiftly in the case, leading to the arrest of three accused, who were subsequently sentenced to life imprisonment.Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news. articles.title: An Oregon artist built a two-storey museum using 800 tons of rock, and its glowing stone artwork and family treasures make it an unusual attraction
articles.summary: An Oregon artist turned an extraordinary building project into a museum filled with glowing stone pictures, bird paintings and family treasures.
articles.body: An Oregon artist turned an extraordinary building project into a museum filled with glowing stone pictures, bird paintings and family treasures. Built using around 800 tons of rock, the two-storey Living Rock Studios houses an unusual collection shaped by religious faith, wildlife and generations of artistic work. Its illuminated pictures are made from thin slices of stone, with light behind them revealing natural colours and patterns. Elsewhere, visitors can explore more than 100 bird paintings, carvings made from native Oregon woods and antiques linked to the family’s history. articles.title: J&K IAS officer Rajeev Ranjan's video abusing woman colleague goes viral: 'I can always talk to you like this'
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: A senior IAS officer Kumar Rajeev Ranjan, administrative secretary, Department of Labour & Employment, Govt.
articles.body: SRINAGAR: A senior IAS officer Kumar Rajeev Ranjan, administrative secretary, Department of Labour & Employment, Govt. of J&K has come under a storm allegedly for calling a woman officer, who was his subordinate as “bloody shit” in a video conference meeting. The purported video of the meeting has gone viral with political parties from ruling National Conference to Bhartiya Janata Party seeking action against the IAS officer.In purported video Ranjan seems to ask question Beenish Wani a JKAS officer currently posted as Assistant Director Employment Ganderbal about the performance. She said she has written to the deputy commissioner and ADC as NRML district officer has stated that targets couldn’t be achieved and they would not cooperate. Ranjan asked her to get it in writing. He also said she should have informed him directly that this happened.“Why do you need NRLM if others are doing the work? Do you only have to write letters and seek the medal? They are just a helping tool, not the main authority,” Ranjan is heard saying in the video. Wani replied that NRLM was needed to assist them. Ranjan told her to “shut up.”When Wani asked him to let her explain and questioned why he was shouting, Ranjan responded, “You are bloody shit. I can always talk to you like this.” Wani objected to being called “shit.” Ranjan then told her to “get out” and asked for an order suspending her to be issued.“To hell with you,” Wani replied.Wani told reporters the incident occurred during a review meeting on Wednesday. She has raised the matter with higher authorities.The labour department has clarified that “it has been brought to notice that a video clip involving the Assistant Director Employment, Ganderbal, and the Secretary, Labour and Employment, is currently in circulation on social media and messaging platforms.”“It is hereby clarified for the general public and media outlets that: 1. AI-Generated Content: The circulating video is entirely AI-generated, fake, and fabricated using digital manipulation techniques. 2. Factual Status: The concerned officer (Assistant Director Employment, Ganderbal) is on leave effective from October 13, 2026, and was not involved in any such interaction as depicted in the video.”In response to it, JKAS officers have condemned the alleged verbal abuse, personal insults and public humiliation of a senior female JKAS officer of the 2015 batch during an official departmental review meeting held (virtually) from the Civil Secretariat, Srinagar, on October 14, 2026.“While the Fraternity unequivocally upholds administrative accountability and performance monitoring, it maintains that no supervisory authority can justify abusive language, intimidation or conduct that undermines the dignity of a serving officer. More disturbing is the department’s subsequent attempt to dismiss the circulating video as AI-generated and fabricated. The video is authentic, as testified by the officer herself and other officials who were present during the virtual meeting,” JKAS officers said in the statement.“The Fraternity considers it deeply unfortunate that, instead of allowing the matter to conclude with an apology and appropriate institutional corrective action, the Administrative Secretary has allegedly chosen to aggravate the controversy through a public clarification that raises further questions about accountability and professional ethics,” the statement said, adding that the JKAS Fraternity calls upon the Lieutenant Governor, the Chief Secretary and the General Administration Department to order an impartial inquiry into both the original incident and the subsequent departmental clarification; ensure that no retaliatory action is taken against the affected officer; and establish effective safeguards against workplace intimidation and abuse of authority.The PDP leader Iltija Mufti wrote on Twitter ‘You are bloody shit, I can always talk to you like this’ - Rajeev Ranjan IAS officer abusing & threatening a lady KAS officer. “How dare you use such derogatory demeaning language? Take your god complex & dirty slurs elsewhere. We won’t tolerate this in Kashmir. Since 2019 KAS & competent Kashmiri IAS officers are deliberately being elbowed out. There is a concerted effort to undermine local officers both in administration & police. Thereby making them subservient to outside officers lording over them. @CM_JnK @manojsinha_ Decency demands this man be suspended immediately. You are quick to fire Kashmiri employees. Hope you use the same yardstick here,” Iltija said.Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi said posted the video on twitter and said “That's how a senior IAS officer in J&K — Administrative Secretary, Labour & Employment — dealt with a woman KAS officer who wouldn't be shouted down in front of a room full of officers. He raised his voice. She raised her dignity. He reached for the only weapon a bully in office has: her job. This is a grown man with a secretary’s chair threatening a woman's career because she asked to be allowed to finish a sentence.”National Conference spokesperson Sarah Hayat Shah called the video shocking. “I salute this woman for standing up for herself and for having the courage to call a spade a spade. Shame on this man for his appalling behaviour!”Congress party also sought action against the officer. The BJP has also said that “the language used by the senior bureaucrat towards his subordinate is completely unbecoming of someone holding such a responsible position, and such behaviour is absolutely unacceptable.” “I do not agree with the argument that the incident is more alarming because the officer on the receiving end was a woman. It would have been equally concerning had the subordinate been a male officer,” BJP spokesman said, seeking action against the official.Ranjan did not answer the phone despite repeated calls.Stay updated with the latest Srinagar news. articles.title: 'We’re done': Zelenskyy defies Trump after Putin attacks Ukraine, says will keep hitting Russian refineries
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said Kyiv will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries after Moscow targeted Kyiv infrastructure, declaring
articles.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said Kyiv will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries after Moscow targeted Kyiv infrastructure, declaring an end to its pause on energy attacks despite pressure from US President Donald Trump to halt them.“The block [on attacking refineries] is out. We’re done,” Financial Times quoted Zelenskyy as saying. He expressed anger over the reported withdrawal of US intelligence support and disruptions to Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite internet service amid intensified Russian attacks.Zelenskyy said Ukraine had paused energy strikes for three days in response to Washington’s requests, while Russia continued attacking Ukrainian energy infrastructure. He said more than 100 civilians had been killed in Russian attacks over the past week.Following his remarks, Russia’s Ryazan governor Pavel Malkov said Ukrainian drone strikes had caused a fire at a refinery owned by state oil company Rosneft. A Ukrainian official said that Kyiv had targeted the facility overnight in retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure.Ukraine’s state energy company Naftogaz also said a Russian strike on one of its gas production facilities east of Kyiv had forced operations to stop.Zelenskyy accuses US of weakening supportThe Ukrainian president said his military had been deprived of US early-warning alerts for incoming ballistic missiles, while reduced Starlink speeds had hampered frontline operations and strikes against Russian military targets.Zelenskyy said Ukrainian military officials had been told by their US counterparts that continued attacks on Russian energy infrastructure would result in intelligence being blocked. The disruption was subsequently presented to Kyiv as a technical issue, he said.“It was not a technical problem, it was the will,” Zelenskyy said.His office later confirmed that Starlink functionality had been restored and speed restrictions lifted. Trump had earlier denied that Washington had cut off intelligence-sharing with Ukraine.Zelenskyy also criticised Washington’s pursuit of business deals with Moscow, arguing that such arrangements could provide Russia with additional resources to sustain its war effort.“The question will be when will the next deal be? Maybe it will be gas. Definitely it will be gas,” he said.Zelenskyy questions Trump’s admiration for PutinAsked about the relationship between Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, Zelenskyy suggested the US president admired leaders who remained in power for decades.“He [Trump] speaks about it openly and loudly that he loves such people and he respects such people. Because for him people who can be leaders 20 years, 30 years, 40 years, it means they can be very strong,” he said.The comments come amid a deepening strain in relations between Kyiv and Washington, Ukraine’s most important security partner. The relationship deteriorated sharply after a public confrontation between Trump and Zelenskyy at the White House in February last year.Zelenskyy said he could consider stopping attacks on Russian energy infrastructure if Washington supplied additional US-made Patriot air defence interceptors, describing this as the minimum he had requested.He also rejected the suggestion that repairing ties with Washington was solely his responsibility. “We didn’t destroy any relationship,” he said.Despite the tensions, Zelenskyy stressed that continued cooperation with the US and Europe was crucial for Ukraine.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Suspension of cellular internet services needed in exigencies’: MHA reply to SC notice
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Continuing with its tough stand against protesters, the home ministry Thursday sought modification of Supreme Court’s Oct 11 order for allowing
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Continuing with its tough stand against protesters, the home ministry Thursday sought modification of Supreme Court’s Oct 11 order for allowing “unhindered internet services” and said exigencies such as disturbance of public order required temporary suspension of cellular internet services, as was the case between 10 pm on Oct 9 to 10 pm on Oct 10 in a 4-km radius of Raisina Hill.In an affidavit filed in response to a contempt of court notice, home secretary Govind Mohan justified Delhi Police’s request for suspension of cellular internet services and said it was “found to be a proportionate measure, having regard to the magnitude of the situation and the need to prevent any disturbance of public order in the national capital”.“The suspension was confined to cellular internet services and did not extend to non-cellular internet services or telecommunications services such as wi-fi and broadband,” he said, emphasising that suspension of such services was considered a recognised measure to maintain public order in appropriate circumstances.The home secretary, Delhi Police commissioner and DMRC chairperson tendered unconditional apology to the court through their affidavits before going on to explain why the steps were taken to prevent unlawful gathering at Jantar Mantar on Oct 10.Though the affidavit conveyed an “unconditional apology“ to the court for the “contempt” charge, it marked a defiant assertion of the Centre’s legal competence and willingness to take strong measures to control "illegal“ protests.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that the “apology” was meant to meet a procedural requirement. “The law is well settled that whenever response is filed pursuant to contempt notice, first sentence we write is that we hereby tender an unconditional apology. And thereafter, we have explained how the contempt is not made out,” he said.“It is with reference to compliance of that law that in every affidavit, this is the first paragraph. Now, in media and social media, things are going on that govt has apologised and they want to say nothing,” he complained.CJI Kant said, “We have not read those media reports, nor are we taking cognisance of any such report.” Justice Bagchi added, “We are neither taking cognisance of the media reports nor your unqualified apology. But by your submissions, it appears to be a qualified apology.”Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar said in his affidavit that permission for the CJP’s Oct 10 protest at Jantar Manor was denied due to past experience of large-scale violence during its July 20 protests, inability of organisers to control supporters and the grave inconvenience caused to general public because of a string of protests from Oct 6-8 that choked central Delhi for days together.Narrating the sensitivity of central Delhi, housing Rashtrapati Bhavan, Parliament, Supreme Court, embassies and other institutions requiring a complex security arrangement as well as measures for maintaining public order, the commissioner said, “No police administration can permit any breach of public order in the national capital, particularly when a call is given by an organisation with a recent history of mob violence, and incidents resulting in injuries to several individuals and the subsequent events of Oct 6, 7, 8.”He added, “Due to all these marches, central Delhi areas got completely choked and there were huge traffic snarls for long hours, resulting in students and innocent citizens getting stuck in traffic jams, resulting in them missing their trains, airlines etc.“The gatherings were very aggressive, fuelled by persons under the cover of ‘freelance journalism’, who were physically harassing policemen, some miscreants were misbehaving with lady police personnel resulting in injuries to over a dozen police personnel.”The commissioner said in compliance with the law laid down by the SC, the police removed illegally gathered people from the site where prohibitory orders were in place but those detained punctured the tyres of buses in which they were kept and broke window shields in acts of violence.All those detained for attempting to protest in violation of prohibitory orders were released after a few hours and were kept in makeshift centres, not police lock-ups, he said. Police provided them with “hot, fresh and good meals” and were permitted to leave after the requirement of detention ceased to exist, he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: A 30-foot-tall cockroach effigy will be burnt alongside those of Ravan, Kumbhkaran and Meghnad during Dussehra celebrations in the national capital this year, with organisers saying the insect will symbolise filth and unhygienic conditions as part of their cleanliness message.The Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee, which organises the Ramlila in Pitampura, said the initiative aims to highlight the need to eliminate filth from homes, neighbourhoods and society at large, in keeping with the Swachh Bharat and Swachh Delhi campaigns.Ashok Goel Devaraha, president of the committee and Model Town BJP MLA, said the decision was intended to reinforce the message of the triumph of good over evil and was not politically motivated.Speaking to ANI, Devaraha said Vijayadashami symbolises the victory of truth over falsehood and righteousness over unrighteousness. He added that the committee had previously burnt effigies representing issues affecting the country, including Naxalism and terrorism.“Keeping these principles in mind, we have also, in the past, burned effigies representing various afflictions plaguing our nation, such as Naxalism or terrorism. This year, our committee has decided to burn an effigy of a cockroach, a symbol of filth,” he said.The effigy will be set alight at the committee grounds in Pitampura. Devaraha described it as a 30-foot-tall structure shaped like a cockroach, adding that the aim was to draw attention to the need to rid homes, neighbourhoods and society of dirt and unhygienic conditions.How did ‘cockroach’ become a political name?The choice of the insect comes amid protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and opposition parties in Delhi, which had been campaigning against former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and is now demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The group staged protests against Pradhan in June and July, including a demonstration at Jantar Mantar and a march towards Parliament on July 20. Pradhan subsequently resigned as education minister in July, while Pralhad Joshi took over the portfolio.The CJP has since returned to the streets over its allegations concerning the electoral roll revision process, joining opposition parties and student organisations in demonstrations. Several activists, students and journalists were detained during protests in the capital.The committee president, however, has denied that the cockroach effigy is politically motivated, maintaining that it is intended to convey a message about cleanliness.Also read: 6,000 cops, 200 CAPF companies: As CJP pushes ahead with Tiranga march, Delhi prepares for a high-security fridayOn May 15, while hearing a case in the Supreme Court, CJI Surya Kant had compared certain individuals with fraudulent degrees to “cockroaches” who become social media or RTI activists to attack the system. The remarks triggered widespread backlash among young people and inspired the satirical “Cockroach Janta Party” (CJP) movement.He later clarified that his oral remarks during a Supreme Court hearing were “misquoted” and later used with “malicious intent” to mislead the country’s youth.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A UK collector paid £20 for a box of comics at a car boot sale and left it in his loft; years later, 47 rare Superman issues inside sold for £63,440
articles.summary: A UK collector who paid just £20 for a box of comics at a car boot sale discovered years later that it contained dozens of exceptionally rare Superman
articles.body: A UK collector who paid just £20 for a box of comics at a car boot sale discovered years later that it contained dozens of exceptionally rare Superman editions. After remaining forgotten in his loft, 47 copies of the 1988 comic 'This Island Bradman' sold for a combined £63,440, including buyer’s fees, at an auction in Surrey on November 4, 2025. The sale, conducted by Ewbank’s Auctions, nearly doubled the collection’s pre-sale estimate of £35,000, according to the auction house and its published results.The collector, who has not been publicly identified, purchased the box roughly a decade earlier from a seller at a car boot sale following a house clearance. He initially had little reason to suspect that the comics were valuable. Describing himself to Ewbank’s as a collector of ephemera rather than comics, he said he had no idea what he had bought.The box was put away in his loft and remained there until the Covid-19 pandemic, when he finally had time to investigate its contents. Online research led him to the unusual story behind the comics and their reputation among Superman enthusiasts. The decisive clue was the number of copies: an account of the original commission mentioned 48 comics being cleared away after an event, matching the number he had found.From a private family gift to a rare Superman comicThe story of 'This Island Bradman' began in 1988, when British businessman Godfrey Bradman commissioned a special Superman comic for his son Daniel’s bar mitzvah. According to Ewbank’s account, building work at the family home had exposed Daniel’s extensive action-comic collection to asbestos, leading to the collection being removed and destroyed.The bespoke comic was commissioned as a replacement gift, with copies intended for distribution to guests at the celebration. Its story featured Daniel Bradman and his friend Andrew Hunt alongside Superman. Rather than creating an entirely separate character or adventure, DC Comics incorporated the personalised story into a Superman comic.The eight-page story was written by David Levin, with artwork by Curt Swan and Angelo Torres. Swan was a major Superman artist whose work helped define the character’s comic-book appearance for decades. The involvement of established creators added to the appeal of an edition that was already unusual because of its private origins.The precise original print run has not been definitively established. Ewbank’s estimated that around 200 copies may have been produced, with more than half distributed to guests. After the event, the remaining copies were reportedly supposed to be discarded. However, a member of the clean-up crew is said to have kept them, preserving a group of comics that subsequently passed through other hands before eventually reaching the car boot sale.Over time, 'This Island Bradman' acquired a reputation as one of the rarest Superman comics. Some proof copies from DC Comics’ offices had reportedly entered circulation, allowing collectors to learn of its existence despite the limited distribution of the original commission. The box found in the UK was particularly significant because it contained the surviving group of 48 copies that enthusiasts had long hoped might reappear.One copy sold online before the auctionAfter researching the comics, the collector began investigating their potential value. He learnt about professional comic grading and tested the market by listing one copy on eBay. According to his account to Ewbank’s, it sold for £750. The comic subsequently appeared on the platform again with a £30,000 asking price, highlighting the gap that can exist between a completed sale and a seller’s hoped-for valuation. An asking price, however, does not establish what a comic is actually worth.The remaining collection was eventually offered through Ewbank’s, a UK auction house based in Surrey. Rather than releasing the comics gradually over several years, the auction house offered 47 copies individually in one sale. Its pre-auction estimate for the collection was £35,000, reflecting the different conditions of the surviving issues.Ewbank’s comic specialist Tom Francis-Duma said the collection presented a rare opportunity for dedicated Superman collectors to acquire an edition that had been difficult to find. The comics varied in condition, with some professionally graded examples reaching CGC 9.6 out of 10. Such grades indicate exceptionally well-preserved copies, although grading scores alone do not determine the final market price.The auction ultimately exceeded expectations. The 47 lots collectively realised £63,440, including buyer’s fees, while the auction house’s later reporting put the hammer total at almost £50,000. The distinction matters because the hammer price is the amount at which the auctioneer sells an item, whereas the final total including buyer’s fees is higher. Ewbank’s catalogue records show that individual copies sold for four-figure sums in many cases, with the most expensive example reaching £2,600 including fees.You use AI every day. articles.summary: The US administration is considering a $335,000 research and advertising campaign in South Africa to understand why fewer white Afrikaners are applying
articles.body: The US administration is considering a $335,000 research and advertising campaign in South Africa to understand why fewer white Afrikaners are applying for refugee status in the United States than officials had expected.According to The Guardian, citing a US state department proposal drafted in August, that the initiative would involve focus groups, a survey of 1,000 Afrikaners and a six-month digital advertising campaign.The proposal said applications had “trended lower than expected” since Afrikaners were allowed to apply directly online in November 2025.The development comes as the administration of President Donald Trump prioritises Afrikaner resettlement while sharply restricting refugee admissions for other groups.Afrikaners are a predominantly Afrikaans-speaking white South African community descended largely from Dutch, French and German settlers who established communities in southern Africa.Trump has repeatedly alleged that white Afrikaners face racial persecution and “white genocide” in South Africa. In February 2025, he signed an executive order directing US officials to prioritise Afrikaner refugee resettlement, citing alleged race-based discrimination and land policies.His administration has also pointed to affirmative action measures and reports of violence against farmers to justify its approach.A US state department spokesperson told The Guardian that Washington continued to process and admit Afrikaners “who are escaping the threat of government-sponsored race-based discrimination”.The South African government has rejected the genocide allegations, maintaining that its land reform and race-based policies are intended to address inequalities created by apartheid rather than persecute white citizens.The dispute has added to tensions between Washington and Pretoria over trade, foreign policy and South Africa's international relationships.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'People of Punjab want answers': Amit Shah targets Bhagwant Mann govt over attacks on anti-drug activists
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Friday targeted the Bhagwant Mann-led Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government over Punjab’s law and order situation,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Friday targeted the Bhagwant Mann-led Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government over Punjab’s law and order situation, citing the killing of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa and the death of a father in Dirba who allegedly consumed poison under pressure.Shah said the two incidents had raised serious questions about the safety of Punjab’s people and announced that the Union home ministry would seek responses from the state government on both cases.“Punjab is grappling today with the rising threats of drugs, gangsterism, and organized crime. The biggest question before the Bhagwant Mann government is: ultimately, who will bear the responsibility for the safety of Punjab's people?” Shah said in a post on X.Referring to Jhota, who was shot dead in Mansa on October 13 while confronting a medical store owner over the alleged sale of synthetic drugs, Shah said the activist’s father had levelled serious allegations against the AAP government and its MLA.“The people of Punjab do not want promises—they want answers; not announcements, but results,” Shah said, urging the state government to take decisive action against drug networks and ensure an impartial investigation into any alleged political patronage extended to criminals.He also flagged the growing threat of organised crime and questioned the protection available to those who speak out against drugs. Shah said the BJP was committed to building a “drug-free, gangster-free, and secure Punjab” if voted to power in the state.Jhota’s killing brings anti-drug campaigners’ safety into focusJhota, 45, was shot dead on October 13 during a confrontation with medical store owner Ashwani Kumar in Mansa. The activist had accused the shop owner of selling synthetic drugs and other prohibited substances. The confrontation was livestreamed on Facebook, and four other people were injured in the firing.Kumar allegedly opened fire inside the shop before pursuing the injured Jhota into the street and firing again. Jhota was hit by three bullets and later died at Mansa Civil Hospital. Kumar was arrested in Rajasthan’s Salasar on October 14, while police also detained an alleged associate accused of helping him flee.Jhota had been campaigning against the alleged sale of intoxicating pills and synthetic drugs in Mansa, recording confrontations with medical store owners and sharing videos on social media.His dispute with Kumar dated back to July 2023, when Jhota allegedly put a garland of shoes around the shop owner’s neck during a public confrontation over the alleged sale of synthetic drugs. A case was registered against Jhota, who spent nearly two months in jail before being released on September 11, 2023, after the complainant approached the court to withdraw the complaint. The case against Kumar over the alleged sale of prohibited substances remained pending.Following Jhota’s killing, his father, Bhim Singh, a retired Army serviceman, refused to cremate his son until those responsible were brought to justice. He vowed to continue his son’s fight against drug peddlers.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: China and North Korea on Thursday officially opened a long-delayed bridge linking their border cities, reviving a major trade route after more than a decade of stalled construction and signalling renewed efforts to strengthen economic ties.The four-lane, 3-km New Yalu River Bridge connects Dandong in northeastern China with Sinuiju in North Korea. Officials from both countries attended the opening ceremony virtually, while trucks bearing Chinese and North Korean flags waited on the bridge.Chinese premier Li Qiang said the two countries’ relationship had entered a “new stage”, describing the crossing as a landmark of their traditional friendship. North Korean premier Pak Thae Song said the bridge would help advance prosperity and improve people’s well-being, according to the countries’ state media.The opening comes as Pyongyang has strengthened its ties with Moscow, including through military support for Russia’s war in Ukraine, prompting questions about Beijing’s influence over its longstanding ally.A decade-long delayThe bridge was completed on the Chinese side in 2014 and was initially expected to open that year. But work on the North Korean side stalled, leaving the crossing unused for more than a decade. The delay fuelled speculation that Pyongyang was wary of becoming more dependent on Beijing or unhappy with China’s support for United Nations sanctions over North Korea’s nuclear programme.The new crossing is expected to ease pressure on the ageing Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, built in 1943, which carries more than 70% of official trade between the two countries. The older bridge accommodates rail and road traffic, but vehicles can cross in only one direction at a time.Even before the new bridge opened, Chinese traders were reportedly rushing to move cargo across the old crossing. A report by Daily NK said shipments surged after China’s National Day holiday, as traders sought to send goods before the new route began operating amid fears of steep tolls and other fees.Authorities have not announced the new bridge’s toll rates. Traders are expected to weigh the cost of using the wider crossing against the older route, meaning improved capacity may not automatically translate into cheaper shipments.Beijing seeks to retain its influenceChina remains North Korea’s largest trading partner and a vital economic lifeline. About 98% of North Korea’s external trade was with China in 2025, according to figures cited in the reports.But Kim Jong Un has increasingly prioritised ties with Russia, sending troops and conventional weapons to support Moscow’s war in Ukraine, apparently in exchange for military and economic assistance. The opening of a road bridge between Russia and North Korea last month underscored that growing partnership.The New Yalu River Bridge could help Beijing reinforce its economic role as Pyongyang broadens its external partnerships. Analysts say it may improve logistics and facilitate trade, although its impact will depend on how the crossing is used and what charges authorities impose.The opening marks a practical change for cross-border commerce and is also a test of how Beijing and Pyongyang manage a relationship shaped by economic dependence, political interests and North Korea’s growing engagement with Moscow.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'You might want to explain. Unless, you want me to': Rahul Gandhi's cryptic post over Rubio's Mumbai visit
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Friday questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi over US secretary of state Marco Rubio’s
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Friday questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi over US secretary of state Marco Rubio’s upcoming Mumbai visit, alleging that officials in the external affairs ministry were "confused" about the developments.“Mr Rubio has summoned his employee to Mumbai. Modi ji, your officials in the external affairs ministry are confused about what's going on. You might want to explain. Unless, of course, you want me to,” Rahul posted on X.His remarks came a day after Congress questioned the Centre’s silence on Rubio’s visit, particularly after US ambassador to India Sergio Gor said American officials expected external affairs minister S Jaishankar to meet Rubio in Mumbai.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh called the ambassador’s statement “extraordinary” and questioned why the announcement of the external affairs minister’s engagements in India was coming from a US official rather than the ministry of external affairs (MEA).“Why is the MEA silent on the external affairs minister's tryst with Mr Rubio in Mumbai?” Ramesh asked, adding that India was learning about the developments from the US ambassador.The US state department announced on Tuesday that Rubio would visit India from October 17 to 22 to strengthen energy cooperation.
